correctness.rationale: Explicit parametrization gives exact section area integral (1), independently checked against Cartesian section integration. Differentiation gives F'=−ξI and stationarity. Exact elementary integral yields F and I logarithmic expansions, plus Q'>0 near zero. Compactness forces every global minimizer for k→0 into that monotone region; all small-k minimizers then agree. Stationarity and controlled remainders give both displayed exponential constants. Finite numerical checks corroborate but are not used to prove quantifiers.

value.rationale: The area-minimizing central slice is a natural extremal geometric quantity. A common axial-alignment intuition fails for every nondegenerate circular bicone, but the departure and area benefit have beyond-all-polynomial, sharp essential-singularity scales. This supplies both a structural rigidity result and an exact stability benchmark for thin bicones, not a parameter restatement.
